_boundary_note: Values are not comparable across differing boundaries or across withdrawal vs consumption; see boundary field and basis. All entries here are onsite. AWS reports withdrawal; Google reports ISO WUE Category 2 consumption; Microsoft reports site water used for humidification and cooling.
_description: Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) coefficients by datacenter location

aws.basis: Amazon Web Services, AWS Cloud sustainability (PUE and WUE tables), 2025 calendar year. Global data center WUE 0.12 L/kWh withdrawn per kWh of IT load. https://sustainability.aboutamazon.com/products-services/aws-cloud. Published directly as a fleet average.

aws-ap-northeast-3.basis: Amazon Web Services, AWS Cloud sustainability, 2025. Asia Pacific (excl. Derived as published Asia Pacific (excl. China) geography WUE applied to the region; arithmetic: value = 1.1.

azure.basis: Microsoft, Measuring energy and water efficiency for Microsoft datacenters, FY25 (1 Jul 2024–30 Jun 2025). Global WUE 0.27 L/kWh = annual liters used for humidification and cooling / IT kWh. https://datacenters.microsoft.com/sustainability/efficiency/. Published directly as a fleet average. Owned-and-operated datacenters operational for 12 months; leased facilities excluded.

azure-centralus.basis: Microsoft, Measuring energy and water efficiency for Microsoft datacenters, FY25 (1 Jul 2024–30 Jun 2025). Published as a continental average applied to a region; arithmetic: value = 0.34.

google.basis: Google, Measuring the environmental impact of delivering AI at Google Scale, 2025, ISO WUE Category 2 (consumptive) for data centers supporting LLM models; 1.15 L/kWh in both 2023 and 2024. https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.15734.
